title: DoorFlow: Scheduling Robots Through Narrow Doors
hints: LoRR 2026: warehouse-like map
Goal: finish as many orders as possible
en: {Good afternoon, everyone.} Our project is based on the **League of Robot Runners 2026** competition, or **LoRR** for short. On a warehouse-like map, robots must finish **as many orders as possible**.
zh: 大家下午好。我们的项目基于 **2026 年机器人跑者联赛（LoRR）**。在一张类似仓库的地图上，机器人要完成**尽可能多的订单**。

segs.en: {Good afternoon, everyone.} Our project is based on the **League of Robot Runners 2026** competition, or **LoRR** for short.
segs.zh: 大家下午好。我们的项目基于 **2026 年机器人跑者联赛（LoRR）**。

segs.en: On a warehouse-like map, robots must finish **as many orders as possible**.
segs.zh: 在一张类似仓库的地图上，机器人要完成**尽可能多的订单**。

title: The task: hundreds of robots, narrow doors
figs: 图 1 背景图
hints: Score = orders finished in 5,000 ticks
3 decisions: assign / route / execute
16 rooms, 31 doors, 1 cell wide, 200–300 robots
Blue path: 8 doors
en: 【指左图】 {The background:} each grey dot is a robot. Robots pick up and deliver orders for **5,000 ticks**, and the score is the **number of orders finished**. 【指右边 1、2、3】 Every tick, the program decides **which robot takes which order, which way it goes, and whether it moves now**. 【指下方数字】 The official room map has **16 rooms and 31 doors**, most only **one cell wide**, and **200 to 300 robots**. 【指蓝色路线】 This one order passes **eight doors**.
zh: 【指左图】背景是：每个灰点是一台机器人。车在 **5000 拍**里不停取货送货，成绩是**完成的订单数**。【指右边 1、2、3】每一拍，程序决定**哪台车接哪单、走哪条路、现在走不走**。【指下方数字】官方房间图有 **16 个房间、31 道门**，大多只有**一格宽**，车有 **200 到 300 台**。【指蓝色路线】这一单要穿过 **8 道门**。

title: The longer it runs, the slower it gets
figs: 图 2 越跑越慢曲线
hints: Ran starter + 2024 champion
Every curve falls
No errors
We start optimizing from this problem
en: We first ran the official starter program and the 2024 champion's method. 【指三组曲线】 Both get **slower the longer they run**. 【指左边 127 和 37】 With the champion's method, orders per 500 ticks fall from **127 at the start to 37 at the end**, averaged over 60 runs. The program reports **no errors**, so **we decided to start our optimization from this problem**.
zh: 我们先跑了官方起始程序和 2024 届冠军的方法。【指三组曲线】两个都是**跑得越久，越慢**。【指左边 127 和 37】用冠军的方法，60 局平均，每 500 拍完成的单数从**开局 127 降到最后 37**。而且程序**没有报错**，**我们想从这个问题着手去优化**。

segs.en: We first ran the official starter program and the 2024 champion's method. 【指三组曲线】 Both get **slower the longer they run**.
segs.zh: 我们先跑了官方起始程序和 2024 届冠军的方法。【指三组曲线】两个都是**跑得越久，越慢**。

segs.en: 【指左边 127 和 37】 With the champion's method, orders per 500 ticks fall from **127 at the start to 37 at the end**, averaged over 60 runs. The program reports **no errors**, so **we decided to start our optimization from this problem**.
segs.zh: 【指左边 127 和 37】用冠军的方法，60 局平均，每 500 拍完成的单数从**开局 127 降到最后 37**。而且程序**没有报错**，**我们想从这个问题着手去优化**。

title: Robots jam at one narrow door
figs: 图 3 第 3000 拍堵门截图
hints: A week to write a monitoring program: replay tick by tick
Over time, many robots jam at one door (97 at tick 3,000 still heading through door 6)
How did earlier work solve this?
For questions: 38% → 86% of orders left need door 6; 3.4–7.0 vs 26 crossings per 500 ticks
en: {To find out what was building up,} we spent **a week writing a monitoring program** to watch the replay **tick by tick**. {Watching the replays, we found that} as time goes on, **many robots jam at one door**. {So how did earlier work try to solve this?}
zh: 为了找出在累积的是什么，我们**花了一周的时间写了一个监测程序**来**一拍一拍**地看回放。通过观看回放，我们发现随着时间的过去，**很多机器人会堵在一个门上**，那么前人是怎么优化这个问题的呢？

segs.en: {To find out what was building up,} we spent **a week writing a monitoring program** to watch the replay **tick by tick**.
segs.zh: 为了找出在累积的是什么，我们**花了一周的时间写了一个监测程序**来**一拍一拍**地看回放。

segs.en: {Watching the replays, we found that} as time goes on, **many robots jam at one door**. {So how did earlier work try to solve this?}
segs.zh: 通过观看回放，我们发现随着时间的过去，**很多机器人会堵在一个门上**，那么前人是怎么优化这个问题的呢？

title: Prior work: four groups of methods
hints: 4 groups: assignment / route guidance / planners (deadlocks & collisions) / jam handling
Each fixes one kind of congestion locally
None avoids congestion at assignment level, whole system
Our question: a global scheduling algorithm?
en: 【依次指四张卡】 Earlier methods fall into four groups. **Order assignment** gives robots close, cheap orders. **Route guidance** makes busy roads cost more, so robots spread out. **Planners** decide which robot moves first, and avoid **deadlocks and collisions**. **Jam handling** keeps some robots idle, or sorts out robots that meet in a narrow passage. 【指底部黄框】 In all the methods we read, each one only fixes **one kind of congestion locally**. None starts from **the whole system** and weighs many factors to **avoid congestion when orders are given out**. {So we wanted to try:} is there a **global scheduling algorithm** that avoids congestion?
zh: 【依次指四张卡】前人的方法可以分成四类。**派单**给车分近的、便宜的单。**选路**让拥挤的路代价更高，把车分散开。**规划**决定哪台车先走，避免**死锁和碰撞**。**拥堵处理**让一部分车闲着，或者处理在窄道里碰上的车。【指底部黄框】在我们读到的所有方法里，每一种都只是**单独在局部优化某种拥塞**，没有一种从**整个系统**出发、同时考虑多个因素**在派单层面去避免拥塞**，所以我们想进行这个尝试，看看有没有一种**全局调度算法**去避免拥塞。

segs.en: 【依次指四张卡】 Earlier methods fall into four groups.
segs.zh: 【依次指四张卡】前人的方法可以分成四类。

segs.en: **Order assignment** gives robots close, cheap orders.
segs.zh: **派单**给车分近的、便宜的单。

segs.en: **Route guidance** makes busy roads cost more, so robots spread out.
segs.zh: **选路**让拥挤的路代价更高，把车分散开。

segs.en: **Planners** decide which robot moves first, and avoid **deadlocks and collisions**.
segs.zh: **规划**决定哪台车先走，避免**死锁和碰撞**。

segs.en: **Jam handling** keeps some robots idle, or sorts out robots that meet in a narrow passage.
segs.zh: **拥堵处理**让一部分车闲着，或者处理在窄道里碰上的车。

segs.en: 【指底部黄框】 In all the methods we read, each one only fixes **one kind of congestion locally**. None starts from **the whole system** and weighs many factors to **avoid congestion when orders are given out**. {So we wanted to try:} is there a **global scheduling algorithm** that avoids congestion?
segs.zh: 【指底部黄框】在我们读到的所有方法里，每一种都只是**单独在局部优化某种拥塞**，没有一种从**整个系统**出发、同时考虑多个因素**在派单层面去避免拥塞**，所以我们想进行这个尝试，看看有没有一种**全局调度算法**去避免拥塞。

title: Where jams happen: our congestion monitor
figs: 拥塞监测程序截图（figures/deck/demo/congestion_monitor.html，第 3000 拍；官方房间图 250 台，种子 9700 / 101；三种选路各跑一局，都不控制门）
hints: Monitor marks every jam red; same map, robots, seeds; only the routing changes
Door 6 jammed 91–94% of the run under all three routings; doors 16–18 too
Orders: champion 609, HN-SPF 435, Fortz–Thorup 612 (one run each)
Why? Two weeks of analysis → hand over to Speaker 3

segs.en: 【指截图】 The monitor **marks every jam in red**. The map, the robots and the seeds are the same; **only the routing algorithm changes**.
segs.zh: 【指截图】监测程序会把**每一处拥塞自动标成红色**。地图、车和种子都一样，**只换了选路的算法**。

segs.en: 【指右边柱状条】 {We found that} **however we changed the routing algorithm**, jams kept happening **at certain places**.
segs.zh: 【指右边柱状条】然后发现，好像**不管如何修改选路的算法**，都无法解决**会在某些地方发生拥塞**的问题。

segs.en: {Why?} We spent **two weeks** analyzing why these versions did not work.
segs.zh: 为什么呢？我们**花了两周**来做为什么失败的分析。

en: 【指截图】 The monitor **marks every jam in red**. The map, the robots and the seeds are the same; **only the routing algorithm changes**. 【指右边柱状条】 {We found that} **however we changed the routing algorithm**, jams kept happening **at certain places**. {Why?} We spent **two weeks** analyzing why these versions did not work.

title: The model: door 6 sets the ceiling
figs: 图 4 地图压成网络；图 7 天花板公式
hints: Model: 16 rooms = nodes, 31 doors = edges; door 6 is a cut
26 ÷ 0.376 ≈ 69, whatever the routes
14 of 15 rerouting methods lowered results; the 15th +0.20% (report Fig. 20)
So: scheduling — how many robots, which side first
en: {Thank you. First, we built a model.} 【指左图】 The **16 rooms are nodes** and the **31 doors are edges**; 【指红线门 6】 **door 6 is a cut**: without it, the four lower-left rooms are cut off. {So why did changing routes not help?} 【指右 1】 The lower-left rooms hold **906 of the 3,614** room cells, which is **25 percent**. 【指右 2】 An order needs door 6 when its two ends are on different sides: **2 times 0.25 times 0.75, about 37.6 percent** of orders; the task file gives 38.5. 【指公式】 Door 6 passes **26 robots** every 500 ticks, so the map can finish at most **26 divided by 0.376, about 69 orders**, whatever routes robots take. {That is why} **14 of 15** rerouting methods we compared lowered results. The real question is **how many robots to send, and which side goes first**: **scheduling**.
zh: 谢谢。我们先建了一个模型。【指左图】**16 个房间是点，31 道门是线**；【指红线门 6】**门 6 是一个割**：没有它，左下 4 个房间就断开了。那为什么改路线没有用？【指右 1】左下房间占 3614 个房间格里的 **906 个**，也就是 906 ÷ 3614 ≈ **25%**。【指右 2】一单两头落在门的两侧，就要过门 6：**2 × 0.2507 × 0.7493 ≈ 37.6%**；任务文件里是 38.5%。【指公式】门 6 每 500 拍过 **26 台**，所以不管车怎么走，整张图最多完成 **26 ÷ 0.376 ≈ 69 单**。所以我们比较过的 15 种换路办法里有 **14 种**都变差。真正的问题是**派多少车、哪边先走**，也就是**调度**。

segs.en: {Thank you. First, we built a model.} 【指左图】 The **16 rooms are nodes** and the **31 doors are edges**; 【指红线门 6】 **door 6 is a cut**: without it, the four lower-left rooms are cut off.
segs.zh: 谢谢。我们先建了一个模型。【指左图】**16 个房间是点，31 道门是线**；【指红线门 6】**门 6 是一个割**：没有它，左下 4 个房间就断开了。

segs.en: {So why did changing routes not help?} 【指右 1】 The lower-left rooms hold **906 of the 3,614** room cells, which is **25 percent**.
segs.zh: 那为什么改路线没有用？【指右 1】左下房间占 3614 个房间格里的 **906 个**，也就是 906 ÷ 3614 ≈ **25%**。

segs.en: 【指右 2】 An order needs door 6 when its two ends are on different sides: **2 times 0.25 times 0.75, about 37.6 percent** of orders; the task file gives 38.5.
【指公式】 Door 6 passes **26 robots** every 500 ticks, so the map can finish at most **26 divided by 0.376, about 69 orders**, whatever routes robots take.
segs.zh: 【指公式】门 6 每 500 拍过 **26 台**，所以不管车怎么走，整张图最多完成 **26 ÷ 0.376 ≈ 69 单**。

segs.en: {That is why} **14 of 15** rerouting methods we compared lowered results. The real question is **how many robots to send, and which side goes first**: **scheduling**.
segs.zh: 所以我们比较过的 15 种换路办法里有 **14 种**都变差。真正的问题是**派多少车、哪边先走**，也就是**调度**。

title: What makes our robots different
figs: 对比表（我们的车 / 计算机网络 / 道路交通，幻灯片上直接画的，阴影 = 和我们的车不一样）
hints: vs networks: they drop packets; vs traffic: no car may wait forever; here one program decides
→ copy neither: we had to build our own new algorithm, DoorFlow
DoorFlow never drops a robot; decides who goes and when; keeps exits clear
en: 【指表格】 Our analysis also showed where we differ from **computer networks** and **road traffic**. A congested network can simply **drop packets**; a robot **cannot be dropped**, and a waiting robot **takes up a cell**. Road traffic cannot leave some cars **standing still forever**, but here we can. And **one program decides every order and move**, not each driver. {So} we **cannot simply copy** network or traffic algorithms; we had to come up with **a completely new algorithm of our own**: **DoorFlow**. {So} DoorFlow **never drops a robot**; it only decides **who goes and when**, and keeps **exits clear**.
zh: 【指表格】同时我们的分析发现了我们和计算机网络和交通流算法不一样的地方：计算机网络里拥塞往往可以直接**丢包**来解决，车**不能因为拥塞被丢弃**；而且等着的车**占着格子**；对于交通来说，交通不能让某些车辆**永远不动**，但是这里我们可以；而且这里**每一单、每一步都由一个程序统一决定**，不像路上每个司机自己选路。所以都**不能直接抄**和借用交通流和计算机网络的算法，我们必须想出**自己全新的算法**：**DoorFlow**。所以我们后来的方向转向了让**出口保持畅通**。

segs.en: 【指表格】 Our analysis also showed where we differ from **computer networks** and **road traffic**. A congested network can simply **drop packets**; a robot **cannot be dropped**, and a waiting robot **takes up a cell**. Road traffic cannot leave some cars **standing still forever**, but here we can. And **one program decides every order and move**, not each driver.
segs.zh: 【指表格】同时我们的分析发现了我们和计算机网络和交通流算法不一样的地方：计算机网络里拥塞往往可以直接**丢包**来解决，车**不能因为拥塞被丢弃**；而且等着的车**占着格子**；对于交通来说，交通不能让某些车辆**永远不动**，但是这里我们可以；而且这里**每一单、每一步都由一个程序统一决定**，不像路上每个司机自己选路。

segs.en: {So} we **cannot simply copy** network or traffic algorithms; we had to come up with **a completely new algorithm of our own**: **DoorFlow**.
segs.zh: 所以都**不能直接抄**和借用交通流和计算机网络的算法，我们必须想出**自己全新的算法**：**DoorFlow**。

segs.en: {So} DoorFlow **never drops a robot**; it only decides **who goes and when**, and keeps **exits clear**.
segs.zh: 所以我们后来的方向转向了让**出口保持畅通**。

title: Scheduling 1: a window for each door
figs: 窗口大小原理图（从“路上的车数 = 过门速率 × 路程时间”推出；这条计数规律在排队论里叫 Little 定律，讲稿不提名字，只写在图注里；理论示意，附门 6 的数字）
hints: Our measure: robots on the way to a door (hold an order through it, not crossed yet) = window
Door 6: 13 per 500 ticks each way = 1 per 38.5 ticks
Trip: 247 ticks free × 2.23 breakdowns ≈ 550 ticks → 550 ÷ 38.5 ≈ 14.3 → 15
Window = door rate × trip time; fewer: door waits; more: queue, block the other side

segs.en: {How many robots should head for door 6 at once?} We came up with a way to **measure how many robots are on the way** to a door: robots that hold an order through it but have not crossed yet. This number is our **window**: it decides **how many orders may cross the door at the same time**.
segs.zh: 同时该有多少车奔向门 6？我们想到一个办法：**衡量在途、会通过某个门口的车有多少**，也就是接了要过这道门的单、还没过门的车。这个数就是我们的**窗口**，用它来决定**同时指派多少个要穿过这道门的任务**。

segs.en: {How big should the window be?} Door 6 lets in **13 robots every 500 ticks** in each direction, **one every 38.5 ticks**. A robot needs **247 ticks** to reach the door on a free path, and random breakdowns make trips **2.23 times** longer: about **550 ticks**. {So} to keep the door busy, we send one robot every 38.5 ticks, and **550 ÷ 38.5 ≈ 14.3** robots are on the way at any moment: the window is **15**.
segs.zh: 窗口该多大？门 6 每个方向每 500 拍能进 **13 台**，也就是**每 38.5 拍一台**。一台车在空路上走到门口要 **247 拍**，随机故障让路程变成 **2.23 倍**，大约 **550 拍**。所以要让门一直有车过，就每 38.5 拍派出一台，路上同时大约有 **550 ÷ 38.5 ≈ 14.3 台**：窗口取 **15**。

segs.en: {In general,} **window = door rate × trip time**. 【指左图上半】 Fewer robots, and the door **waits**; 【指左图下半】 more, and the extras only **queue**, and waiting robots **block the other side**.
segs.zh: 一般地说，**窗口 = 过门速率 × 路程时间**。【指左图上半】车少了，门就**等车**；【指左图下半】车多了，多出来的只会**排队**，还会**挡住对面**。

en: {How many robots should head for door 6 at once?} We came up with a way to **measure how many robots are on the way** to a door: robots that hold an order through it but have not crossed yet. This number is our **window**: it decides **how many orders may cross the door at the same time**. {How big should the window be?} Door 6 lets in **13 robots every 500 ticks** in each direction, **one every 38.5 ticks**. A robot needs **247 ticks** to reach the door on a free path, and random breakdowns make trips **2.23 times** longer: about **550 ticks**. {So} to keep the door busy, we send one robot every 38.5 ticks, and **550 ÷ 38.5 ≈ 14.3** robots are on the way at any moment: the window is **15**. {In general,} **window = door rate × trip time**. 【指左图上半】 Fewer robots, and the door **waits**; 【指左图下半】 more, and the extras only **queue**, and waiting robots **block the other side**.
zh: 同时该有多少车奔向门 6？我们想到一个办法：**衡量在途、会通过某个门口的车有多少**，也就是接了要过这道门的单、还没过门的车。这个数就是我们的**窗口**，用它来决定**同时指派多少个要穿过这道门的任务**。窗口该多大？门 6 每个方向每 500 拍能进 **13 台**，也就是**每 38.5 拍一台**。一台车在空路上走到门口要 **247 拍**，随机故障让路程变成 **2.23 倍**，大约 **550 拍**。所以要让门一直有车过，就每 38.5 拍派出一台，路上同时大约有 **550 ÷ 38.5 ≈ 14.3 台**：窗口取 **15**。一般地说，**窗口 = 过门速率 × 路程时间**。【指左图上半】车少了，门就**等车**；【指左图下半】车多了，多出来的只会**排队**，还会**挡住对面**。

title: Scheduling 1: the quota for each door
figs: 图 9 在途车与过门数
图 8 名额公式
hints: Count: holds a door-6 order, not crossed, even far away; full → order that does not cross
One window for all (round 25): +0.53% on the champion (small)
Per door & direction (rounds 28–29) → +29.1% alone (17 room-map instances)
Size: 8 too tight, 32+ jams → formula 15 in / 10 out (round 41), no worse than hand-tuned (+0.63%)
No control 211 → 3; quota ~25 (knee) → 26

segs.en: When a door's quota is full, the next robot gets **an order that does not need the door**.
segs.zh: 某道门的名额满了，下一台车就派**一单不用过这道门的**。

segs.en: Counting all robots together gained only **0.53 percent**. Counting **per door and per direction** gained **29.1 percent** on its own, on 17 room-map instances.
segs.zh: 把所有车一起数，只多了 **0.53%**。改成**按门、按方向**数，单独就多了 **29.1%**（17 个房间图实例）。

segs.en: 【指下方公式】 Hand-tuned sizes were too tight at 8 and jammed at 32 or more; the formula gives **15 in** and **10 out**, as good as the best hand-tuned value.
segs.zh: 【指下方公式】手调时 8 台太紧，32 台以上又会堵；公式给出**进 15 台、出 10 台**，和手调的最好值一样好。

segs.en: 【指左图】 With no control, **211** robots head for the door and **3** get through; with the quota, about **25**, at the knee, and **26** get through.
segs.zh: 【指左图】不管门时 **211 台**车奔向门、只过 **3 台**；用名额后大约 25 台，正好在拐点上，能过 **26 台**。

en: When a door's quota is full, the next robot gets **an order that does not need the door**. Counting all robots together gained only **0.53 percent**. Counting **per door and per direction** gained **29.1 percent** on its own, on 17 room-map instances. 【指下方公式】 Hand-tuned sizes were too tight at 8 and jammed at 32 or more; the formula gives **15 in** and **10 out**, as good as the best hand-tuned value. 【指左图】 With no control, **211** robots head for the door and **3** get through; with the quota, about **25**, at the knee, and **26** get through.
zh: 某道门的名额满了，下一台车就派**一单不用过这道门的**。把所有车一起数，只多了 **0.53%**。改成**按门、按方向**数，单独就多了 **29.1%**（17 个房间图实例）。【指下方公式】手调时 8 台太紧，32 台以上又会堵；公式给出**进 15 台、出 10 台**，和手调的最好值一样好。【指左图】不管门时 **211 台**车奔向门、只过 **3 台**；用名额后大约 25 台，正好在拐点上，能过 **26 台**。

title: Scheduling 2: one direction at a time
figs: 门口规则详图 A：缓冲区示意和换向规则（演讲专用，从 fig_door_rule_deck.png 切出）
hints: 1-cell door: one direction at a time
Waiting side queues at the buffer edge + lowest priority → +27.6% alone (17 room-map instances)

segs.en: {Our second rule is} the **door rule**: a one-cell door carries **one direction at a time**.
segs.zh: 第二条规则是**门口规则**：一格宽的门**一次只走一个方向**。

segs.en: 【指左图 A】 The waiting side **queues at the edge of a buffer** around the door, and robots held by the rule get the **lowest priority**, so the exit stays clear. Alone, this rule gained **27.6 percent**.
segs.zh: 【指左图 A】等着的一边**在门口缓冲区的边上排队**，被规则拦住的车排到**最低优先级**，出口就一直是空的。单独用这条规则就多了 **27.6%**。

en: {Our second rule is} the **door rule**: a one-cell door carries **one direction at a time**. 【指左图 A】 The waiting side **queues at the edge of a buffer** around the door, and robots held by the rule get the **lowest priority**, so the exit stays clear. Alone, this rule gained **27.6 percent**.
zh: 第二条规则是**门口规则**：一格宽的门**一次只走一个方向**。【指左图 A】等着的一边**在门口缓冲区的边上排队**，被规则拦住的车排到**最低优先级**，出口就一直是空的。单独用这条规则就多了 **27.6%**。

title: Scheduling 2: how long does the door take?
figs: 门 6 过门间隔的实测（演讲专用：5 局仿真，官方房间图 250 台，DoorFlow，1255 次过门；figures/deck/demo/door_timing.py）
hints: Measured: 5 runs (seeds 9700–9704), official map, 250 robots, DoorFlow, 1255 crossings of door 6
Same direction: mostly 6 or 9 ticks = 2 or 3 moves (3 ticks per move); median 10
Switch: median 34 ticks (door + 4-cell buffer must empty) → +24 per switch

segs.en: {How many ticks does the door need per robot? We measured it.} We ran **5 simulations**: official map, 250 robots, DoorFlow, 5,000 ticks each, and timed all **1,255 crossings** of door 6.
segs.zh: 门每过一台车要多少拍？我们直接测：跑了 **5 局仿真**（官方地图、250 台车、DoorFlow，每局 5000 拍），记下门 6 全部 **1255 次过门**的时间。

segs.en: 【指左图】 In the same direction, the next robot usually comes **6 or 9 ticks** later: that is **2 or 3 moves**, because one move takes **3 ticks** in this competition. The median is **10 ticks**.
segs.zh: 【指左图】同一个方向，下一台车通常隔 **6 拍或 9 拍**，也就是 **2 步或 3 步**，因为比赛里走一步要 **3 拍**。中位数是 **10 拍**。

segs.en: 【指右图】 When the door switches direction, the first robot comes a median of **34 ticks** later, because the door and the 4-cell buffer must empty first. {So} every switch costs about **24 extra ticks**.
segs.zh: 【指右图】门换方向时，第一台车的中位数要隔 **34 拍**，因为门和 4 格缓冲区要先清空。所以每换一次方向，大约多花 **24 拍**。

en: {How many ticks does the door need per robot? We measured it.} We ran **5 simulations**: official map, 250 robots, DoorFlow, 5,000 ticks each, and timed all **1,255 crossings** of door 6. 【指左图】 In the same direction, the next robot usually comes **6 or 9 ticks** later: that is **2 or 3 moves**, because one move takes **3 ticks** in this competition. The median is **10 ticks**. 【指右图】 When the door switches direction, the first robot comes a median of **34 ticks** later, because the door and the 4-cell buffer must empty first. {So} every switch costs about **24 extra ticks**.
zh: 门每过一台车要多少拍？我们直接测：跑了 **5 局仿真**（官方地图、250 台车、DoorFlow，每局 5000 拍），记下门 6 全部 **1255 次过门**的时间。【指左图】同一个方向，下一台车通常隔 **6 拍或 9 拍**，也就是 **2 步或 3 步**，因为比赛里走一步要 **3 拍**。中位数是 **10 拍**。【指右图】门换方向时，第一台车的中位数要隔 **34 拍**，因为门和 4 格缓冲区要先清空。所以每换一次方向，大约多花 **24 拍**。

title: Scheduling 2: serve one side until it is empty
figs: 门速度曲线（演讲专用：U(n) = nh / ((n−1)h + s)，h = 10、s = 34 用上一页的实测中位数）
hints: Door = server with 2 queues, one per direction
Turn of n: 34 + 10(n − 1) ticks; without switching 10n
Tests: fixed timetable −5.0%, −6.4%; until empty vs ≤ 80 steps: +1.1% (mostly new room maps)

segs.en: The door is like a **server with two queues**, one per direction: which queue should it serve, and for how long?
segs.zh: 门就像一个**有两个队列的服务台**，每个方向一个队列：先服务哪个队列、服务多久？

segs.en: 【指公式】 {With the measured numbers,} a turn of **n** robots takes **34 + 10 × (n − 1)** ticks, while **10 × n** would be enough without switching. {So} the door runs at **U(n) = 10n ÷ (34 + 10(n − 1))** of its top speed. 【指曲线左端】 One robot per turn: **10 ÷ 34 = 29 percent**. 【指 n = 10】 Ten per turn: **100 ÷ 124 = 81 percent**.

{So} we serve one side **until it is empty**; in our runs a turn let through **9.3 robots** on average. {We also tested it:} switching on a fixed timetable lost **5.0 and 6.4 percent**, and serving until empty beat a limit of 80 steps per turn by **1.1 percent**, mostly on new room maps.
segs.zh: 所以让一边**走空再换**；在我们的仿真里，平均每轮放 **9.3 台**。我们也做了实验：按固定时间表换向少了 **5.0% 和 6.4%**；走空再换比每轮最多放 80 步多 **1.1%**，主要来自新生成的房间图。

en: The door is like a **server with two queues**, one per direction: which queue should it serve, and for how long? 【指公式】 {With the measured numbers,} a turn of **n** robots takes **34 + 10 × (n − 1)** ticks, while **10 × n** would be enough without switching. {So} the door runs at **U(n) = 10n ÷ (34 + 10(n − 1))** of its top speed. 【指曲线左端】 One robot per turn: **10 ÷ 34 = 29 percent**. 【指 n = 10】 Ten per turn: **100 ÷ 124 = 81 percent**. {So} we serve one side **until it is empty**; in our runs a turn let through **9.3 robots** on average. {We also tested it:} switching on a fixed timetable lost **5.0 and 6.4 percent**, and serving until empty beat a limit of 80 steps per turn by **1.1 percent**, mostly on new room maps.
zh: 门就像一个**有两个队列的服务台**，每个方向一个队列：先服务哪个队列、服务多久？【指公式】代入实测的数：一轮放 **n** 台要 **34 + 10 × (n − 1)** 拍，不换向时 **10 × n** 拍就够。所以门的速度是最快速度的 **U(n) = 10n ÷ (34 + 10(n − 1))**。【指曲线左端】每轮只放 1 台：**10 ÷ 34 = 29%**。【指 n = 10】每轮放 10 台：**100 ÷ 124 = 81%**。所以让一边**走空再换**；在我们的仿真里，平均每轮放 **9.3 台**。我们也做了实验：按固定时间表换向少了 **5.0% 和 6.4%**；走空再换比每轮最多放 80 步多 **1.1%**，主要来自新生成的房间图。

title: Scheduling 2: how big should the buffer be?
figs: 门口规则详图 B、C：缓冲区大小扫描（12 个开发实例）；门 6 每过一台 18.7 拍的分解（第 52 轮 669 次过门）；下限 ⌈9 ÷ 3⌉ = 3 格的公式见 netmac.cpp 第 59–62 行注释（第 57 轮）
hints: Exit: a robot every 9–10 ticks, 3 ticks per move → ~3 cells → wait at least 3 cells back
Sweep (12 dev, vs 4): 1 cell −9.0%, 2 −5.2%, 3 even (confirm −2.64%, deadlocks 11 → 29), 6 −4.2% → 4 = minimum + 1
18.7 ticks per crossing (round 52); breakdowns 4.8; 500 ÷ 18.7 ≈ 26.7 ≈ 26
Hand over to Speaker 4

segs.en: 【指上图 B】 {How big should the buffer be?} Robots come out of the door every **9 to 10 ticks**, and one move takes **3 ticks**, so a robot that just came out is only about **3 cells** away when the next one comes out. {So} the waiting side must stand **at least 3 cells** back, or robots coming out get stuck.
segs.zh: 【指上图 B】缓冲区该多大？门里每 **9 到 10 拍**出来一台车，走一步要 **3 拍**，所以下一台出来时，前一台只走出大约 **3 格**。所以等着的一边至少要退后 **3 格**，不然出来的车会被堵住。

segs.en: {Then we tested} 1 to 6 cells on **12 development instances**: 1 and 2 cells lost **9.0 and 5.2 percent**; 3 cells looked even, but a confirmation test lost **2.64 percent**, with deadlocked runs up from **11 to 29**; 6 cells lost **4.2 percent**, as the queue blocked other doors. {So we use} **4 cells**: the minimum plus one.
segs.zh: 然后我们实测了 1 到 6 格（**12 个开发实例**）：1 格、2 格分别少 **9.0%、5.2%**；3 格看起来持平，但确认测试少 **2.64%**，堵死的局从 **11 局增到 29 局**；6 格少 **4.2%**，因为排队的车挡住了别的门。所以用 **4 格**：下限再多留 1 格。

segs.en: 【指下图 C】 The buffer also keeps **random pauses** out of the exit: each robot needs **18.7 ticks** at door 6, **4.8** of them breakdowns; and **500 ÷ 18.7 ≈ 26.7** is where the door's **26** comes from. {Over to Speaker 4.}
segs.zh: 【指下图 C】缓冲区也让**随机暂停**不会堵在出口：门 6 每过一台要 **18.7 拍**，其中 **4.8 拍**是故障；**500 ÷ 18.7 ≈ 26.7**，这就是门每 500 拍过 **26 台**的来历。下面交给讲者 4。

en: 【指上图 B】 {How big should the buffer be?} Robots come out of the door every **9 to 10 ticks**, and one move takes **3 ticks**, so a robot that just came out is only about **3 cells** away when the next one comes out. {So} the waiting side must stand **at least 3 cells** back, or robots coming out get stuck. {Then we tested} 1 to 6 cells on **12 development instances**: 1 and 2 cells lost **9.0 and 5.2 percent**; 3 cells looked even, but a confirmation test lost **2.64 percent**, with deadlocked runs up from **11 to 29**; 6 cells lost **4.2 percent**, as the queue blocked other doors. {So we use} **4 cells**: the minimum plus one. 【指下图 C】 The buffer also keeps **random pauses** out of the exit: each robot needs **18.7 ticks** at door 6, **4.8** of them breakdowns; and **500 ÷ 18.7 ≈ 26.7** is where the door's **26** comes from. {Over to Speaker 4.}
zh: 【指上图 B】缓冲区该多大？门里每 **9 到 10 拍**出来一台车，走一步要 **3 拍**，所以下一台出来时，前一台只走出大约 **3 格**。所以等着的一边至少要退后 **3 格**，不然出来的车会被堵住。然后我们实测了 1 到 6 格（**12 个开发实例**）：1 格、2 格分别少 **9.0%、5.2%**；3 格看起来持平，但确认测试少 **2.64%**，堵死的局从 **11 局增到 29 局**；6 格少 **4.2%**，因为排队的车挡住了别的门。所以用 **4 格**：下限再多留 1 格。【指下图 C】缓冲区也让**随机暂停**不会堵在出口：门 6 每过一台要 **18.7 拍**，其中 **4.8 拍**是故障；**500 ÷ 18.7 ≈ 26.7**，这就是门每 500 拍过 **26 台**的来历。下面交给讲者 4。

hints: Planning round: count per door & direction; give an order only if every door it crosses has room
Every tick: door rule; other side steps back; blocked → lowest priority
Grey lines = 2 safety nets, from the random-door test (later)

segs.en: {Thank you. Here is DoorFlow in pseudocode.} 【指上半】 Every planning round, we count the robots heading for each door and direction, and give an order only if every door it crosses still has room.

segs.en: 【指下半】 Every tick, the door rule decides which side may move and pushes the other side back; robots blocked by it get the lowest priority. 【指灰色两行】 The grey lines are two safety nets from our random-door test{, which I will show soon}.

Here is DoorFlow in pseudocode.} 【指上半】 Every planning round, we count the robots heading for each door and direction, and give an order only if every door it crosses still has room. 【指下半】 Every tick, the door rule decides which side may move and pushes the other side back; robots blocked by it get the lowest priority. 【指灰色两行】 The grey lines are two safety nets from our random-door test{, which I will show soon}.

title: The hardest part: does it run as we meant?
figs: 回放演示动图（每处拥堵自动变红；本项目模拟器，种子 9700 / 101）
hints: Pseudocode is short; hardest: real code doing what we meant → most of our time
Rounds 1–8 void: fixed seed + unset variable; 54 runs, only 5 identical
+6.8% from a mechanism that never switched on (picked no door in 32 instances)
Executor bug: only visible tick by tick
Same congestion monitor on our own code: 1,130 vs 609 orders in this run

segs.en: {The pseudocode looks short.} The hardest part was writing the real code, and then checking that the robots **really did what we meant**. This took most of our time.
segs.zh: 伪代码看起来很短。最难的是写出真正的代码，再检查车是不是**真的按我们的意思在走**。我们大部分时间都花在这里。

segs.en: 【指左边三张卡】 {For example,} our first eight rounds were void: a fixed planner seed and an unset variable meant the same program, run **54 times**, gave the same result only **5 times**. One version gained **6.8 percent**, but its mechanism **never switched on**.
segs.zh: 【指左边三张卡】比如前 8 轮结果全部作废：规划器种子写死、一个变量没初始化，同一个程序跑 **54 次**只有 **5 次**结果相同。有一版多了 **6.8%**，但它的机制**根本没启动**。

segs.en: 【指右边动图】 We used the same congestion monitor to check our own code: without door control, red spreads around door 6; with DoorFlow, the door keeps flowing, **1,130 orders instead of 609** in this run.
segs.zh: 【指右边动图】我们也用同一个拥塞监测程序检查自己的代码：不管门时，门 6 周围一片红；用 DoorFlow，门一直在流动，这一局 **1130 单对 609 单**。

en: {The pseudocode looks short.} The hardest part was writing the real code, and then checking that the robots **really did what we meant**. This took most of our time. 【指左边三张卡】 {For example,} our first eight rounds were void: a fixed planner seed and an unset variable meant the same program, run **54 times**, gave the same result only **5 times**. One version gained **6.8 percent**, but its mechanism **never switched on**. 【指右边动图】 We used the same congestion monitor to check our own code: without door control, red spreads around door 6; with DoorFlow, the door keeps flowing, **1,130 orders instead of 609** in this run.
zh: 伪代码看起来很短。最难的是写出真正的代码，再检查车是不是**真的按我们的意思在走**。我们大部分时间都花在这里。【指左边三张卡】比如前 8 轮结果全部作废：规划器种子写死、一个变量没初始化，同一个程序跑 **54 次**只有 **5 次**结果相同。有一版多了 **6.8%**，但它的机制**根本没启动**。【指右边动图】我们也用同一个拥塞监测程序检查自己的代码：不管门时，门 6 周围一片红；用 DoorFlow，门一直在流动，这一局 **1130 单对 609 单**。

title: Does it only work on this map? Random doors
figs: 换图测试图（8 张随机门房间图 × 2 种车数），讲第一栏
hints: Finally: not tuned to one door? random-door program, 8 new room maps
199 / 249 robots, 640 runs: wins every map, +86.9%
Two new problems → two safety nets (next slide)

segs.en: {Finally,} to make sure DoorFlow is not tuned to this one door, we wrote a program that **places doors at random**, built **8 new room maps**, and checked **what else the algorithm needs**.
segs.zh: 最后，为了确认 DoorFlow 不只是针对这一道门的优化，我们写了一个**随机放门**的程序，造了 **8 张新的房间图**，看看算法**还需要什么**。

segs.en: 【指左图第一栏】 On each map we ran **199 and 249 robots**, **640 runs** in total. Compared with the same base, our method **won on every map**, by **86.9 percent** on average.
segs.zh: 【指左图第一栏】每张图跑 **199 台和 249 台**两种车数，一共 **640 局**。和同一底座比，我们的方法**每张图都赢**，平均多 **86.9%**。

segs.en: {But} the new maps also showed **two problems** that the official map does not have, so we added **two safety nets**.

en: {Finally,} to make sure DoorFlow is not tuned to this one door, we wrote a program that **places doors at random**, built **8 new room maps**, and checked **what else the algorithm needs**. 【指左图第一栏】 On each map we ran **199 and 249 robots**, **640 runs** in total. Compared with the same base, our method **won on every map**, by **86.9 percent** on average. {But} the new maps also showed **two problems** that the official map does not have, so we added **two safety nets**.
zh: 最后，为了确认 DoorFlow 不只是针对这一道门的优化，我们写了一个**随机放门**的程序，造了 **8 张新的房间图**，看看算法**还需要什么**。【指左图第一栏】每张图跑 **199 台和 249 台**两种车数，一共 **640 局**。和同一底座比，我们的方法**每张图都赢**，平均多 **86.9%**。不过，新图也暴露了官方图上没有的**两个问题**，所以我们又加了**两个兜底**。

title: Two safety nets from the new maps
figs: 窄门口拥堵图（演讲专用：随机门图 GenH，249 台，种子 11901 / 172，有无全图上限各跑一局；figures/deck/demo/narrow_spots.py）
hints: Global cap: jams at narrow doorways (circled); no cap: all 249 hold orders, 818 orders; cap 177: 1277 (seeds 11901 / 172)
GenH 249, 10 paired runs: −16.9% without the cap
Deadlock 1,114 → 700 → watchdog 300 ticks, relax the rule
Watchdog: no measurable effect on these 8; earlier +2.30% on 15 generated room-map instances

segs.en: 【指左图】 {First,} the **global cap**. {On this new map,} jams formed at **narrow doorways** (circled). Without a cap, all **249** robots held orders, and this run finished **818** orders; with the cap, at most **177** held orders, and the same run finished **1,277**. Over 10 runs, the cap was worth **16.9 percent**.
segs.zh: 【指左图】第一个是**全图上限**。在这张新图上，车堵在了**几个窄门口**（虚线圈）。没有上限时，**249 台**车全都接着单，这一局只完成 **818 单**；加上上限，同时接单的最多 **177 台**，同一局完成 **1277 单**。跑 10 局平均，上限值 **16.9%**。

segs.en: 【指右下卡片】 {Second,} rare **deadlocks**: two doors one step apart locked each other, and one run fell from **1,114 to 700** orders. A **watchdog** lets a robot that has waited **300 ticks** at an idle door ignore the rule for one tick; we never remove a robot.
segs.zh: 【指右下卡片】第二，少见的**死锁**：两道只隔一步的门互相锁住，有一局完成数从 **1114 单掉到 700 单**。**看门狗**让在没人进的门口等满 **300 拍**的车，这一拍可以不守门口规则；我们从不拿掉车。

segs.en: Deadlocks are rare: no measurable effect on these maps, and **+2.30 percent** in an earlier test on 15 generated room-map instances.
segs.zh: 死锁很少见：在这些图上测不出作用，在更早一次 15 个生成房间图实例的测试里多了 **2.30%**。

Over 10 runs, the cap was worth **16.9 percent**. 【指右下卡片】 {Second,} rare **deadlocks**: two doors one step apart locked each other, and one run fell from **1,114 to 700** orders. title: Which parts matter?
figs: 图 16 逐项拿掉与加上（演讲专用版：同一组 600 局数据，标签改成不带网络术语的说法）
hints: 600 runs, remove one part
Door rule −25.6, quota −13.6
Door rule alone +29.7, quota alone +29.3, everything +76.4
Quota = how many; door rule = how they pass
en: {Which parts matter most?} 【指左边红条】 In **600 runs**, we removed one part at a time. Without the **door rule**, we lose **25.6 percent**; without the **quota**, **13.6 percent**. 【指右边蓝条】 Added alone, the door rule gives **29.7 percent** and the quota **29.3 percent**; everything together gives **76.4 percent**. 【指黄框】 **The quota decides how many robots come, and the door rule decides how they pass**.
zh: 哪些部分最重要？【指左边红条】我们跑了 **600 局**，每次拿掉一项：拿掉门口规则少 **25.6%**，拿掉名额少 **13.6%**。【指右边蓝条】单独加门口规则多 **29.7%**，单独加名额多 **29.3%**，两个一起多 **76.4%**。【指黄框】简单说，**名额管来多少车，门口规则管车怎么过**。

segs.zh: 哪些部分最重要？【指左边红条】我们跑了 **600 局**，每次拿掉一项：拿掉门口规则少 **25.6%**，拿掉名额少 **13.6%**。

segs.en: 【指右边蓝条】 Added alone, the door rule gives **29.7 percent** and the quota **29.3 percent**; everything together gives **76.4 percent**.
segs.zh: 【指右边蓝条】单独加门口规则多 **29.7%**，单独加名额多 **29.3%**，两个一起多 **76.4%**。

segs.en: 【指黄框】 **The quota decides how many robots come, and the door rule decides how they pass**.
segs.zh: 【指黄框】简单说，**名额管来多少车，门口规则管车怎么过**。

title: Lessons: why DoorFlow looks like this
figs: 五条经验卡片（幻灯片上；数字取自报告第九节）
hints: Lessons from all versions on slide 6
Door 6 cannot be bypassed: 14 of 15 rerouting lower → control how many, not where
Cannot drop, take cells → only decide who goes and when
Waiting less ≠ crossing more: credit flow −2.74% → judge by orders finished
Few maps only (7 of 69) → confirm on new maps; measure first (38 of 69 stopped before code)
en: Looking back at all the versions on slide 6, five lessons explain **why DoorFlow ended up this way**. 【指第一张卡】 Door 6 cannot be bypassed: **14 of 15** rerouting methods lowered results, so we control **how many robots go**, not where. 【指第二张卡】 Robots cannot be dropped and take up cells, so methods built on dropping or buffering do not carry over; we only decide **who goes and when**. 【指第三张卡】 Waiting less is not crossing more: **hop-by-hop credit flow** cut waiting but lowered results by **2.74 percent**, so we judge every change by orders finished. 【指第四张卡】 Gains on a few maps do not count: **7 of 69** ideas passed development but not new maps, so we confirm on new maps. 【指第五张卡】 {And} we **measure the possible gain first**: **38 of 69** ideas stopped there, before any code.
zh: 回头看第 6 页的所有版本，有五条经验解释了 **DoorFlow 为什么是现在这个样子**。【指第一张卡】门 6 绕不开：15 种换路办法里 **14 种**都变差，所以我们管**派多少车**，不管走哪条路。【指第二张卡】车不能丢、还占着格子，所以靠“丢掉”或“先存起来”的办法都用不上；我们只决定**谁走、什么时候走**。【指第三张卡】等得少不等于过得多：**逐跳信用流控**让车等得少了，结果却少了 **2.74%**，所以每项改动都按完成的单数来判断。【指第四张卡】只在少数图上有提升不算数：69 种里有 **7 种**过了开发测试、换新图就不行，所以要换新图确认。【指第五张卡】而且**先量能省多少**：69 种里有 **38 种**量完就停了，没写代码。

segs.en: Looking back at all the versions on slide 6, five lessons explain **why DoorFlow ended up this way**.
segs.zh: 回头看第 6 页的所有版本，有五条经验解释了 **DoorFlow 为什么是现在这个样子**。

segs.en: 【指第一张卡】 Door 6 cannot be bypassed: **14 of 15** rerouting methods lowered results, so we control **how many robots go**, not where.
segs.zh: 【指第一张卡】门 6 绕不开：15 种换路办法里 **14 种**都变差，所以我们管**派多少车**，不管走哪条路。

segs.en: 【指第二张卡】 Robots cannot be dropped and take up cells, so methods built on dropping or buffering do not carry over; we only decide **who goes and when**.
segs.zh: 【指第二张卡】车不能丢、还占着格子，所以靠“丢掉”或“先存起来”的办法都用不上；我们只决定**谁走、什么时候走**。

segs.en: 【指第三张卡】 Waiting less is not crossing more: **hop-by-hop credit flow** cut waiting but lowered results by **2.74 percent**, so we judge every change by orders finished.
segs.zh: 【指第三张卡】等得少不等于过得多：**逐跳信用流控**让车等得少了，结果却少了 **2.74%**，所以每项改动都按完成的单数来判断。

segs.en: 【指第四张卡】 Gains on a few maps do not count: **7 of 69** ideas passed development but not new maps, so we confirm on new maps.
segs.zh: 【指第四张卡】只在少数图上有提升不算数：69 种里有 **7 种**过了开发测试、换新图就不行，所以要换新图确认。

segs.en: 【指第五张卡】 {And} we **measure the possible gain first**: **38 of 69** ideas stopped there, before any code.
segs.zh: 【指第五张卡】而且**先量能省多少**：69 种里有 **38 种**量完就停了，没写代码。

title: Conclusion
hints: DoorFlow: not smarter robots; how many per door + which side first
Routes no, scheduling yes: +140.5% vs official starter (official room map)
Real warehouse: quota per direction + one direction at a time
Simulation only; re-measure for new layouts
Thank you, questions
en: {To conclude.} 【指 1】 **DoorFlow does not make each robot smarter**; it controls **how many robots head for a door, and which side goes first**. 【指 2】 Changing routes did not help, but **scheduling** did: on the official room map, **140.5 percent** more orders than the official starter program. 【指 3】 For a real warehouse, this means **a quota for each direction when orders are given out, and one direction at a time in narrow aisles**. 【指 4】 Our limits: all results come **from simulation**, and the numbers must be **measured again for a new layout**. Thank you. We are happy to take your questions.
zh: 总结一下。【指 1】**DoorFlow 没有让每台车更聪明**，而是管住**有多少车奔向一道门、哪边先走**。【指 2】改路线没有用，**调度**有用：在官方房间图上，比官方起始程序多完成 **140.5%**。【指 3】放到真实仓库里，就是**派单时每个方向设一个名额，窄巷一次只放一个方向**。【指 4】局限是：所有结果都**来自仿真**，换一种布局要**重新测参数**。谢谢大家，欢迎提问。

segs.en: {To conclude.} 【指 1】 **DoorFlow does not make each robot smarter**; it controls **how many robots head for a door, and which side goes first**.
segs.zh: 总结一下。【指 1】**DoorFlow 没有让每台车更聪明**，而是管住**有多少车奔向一道门、哪边先走**。

segs.en: 【指 2】 Changing routes did not help, but **scheduling** did: on the official room map, **140.5 percent** more orders than the official starter program.
segs.zh: 【指 2】改路线没有用，**调度**有用：在官方房间图上，比官方起始程序多完成 **140.5%**。

segs.en: 【指 3】 For a real warehouse, this means **a quota for each direction when orders are given out, and one direction at a time in narrow aisles**.
segs.zh: 【指 3】放到真实仓库里，就是**派单时每个方向设一个名额，窄巷一次只放一个方向**。

segs.en: 【指 4】 Our limits: all results come **from simulation**, and the numbers must be **measured again for a new layout**.
segs.zh: 【指 4】局限是：所有结果都**来自仿真**，换一种布局要**重新测参数**。

segs.en: Thank you. We are happy to take your questions.
segs.zh: 谢谢大家，欢迎提问。
